basis: Adrenal insufficiency, achalasia and alacrima define the triad; neurologic dysfunction affects roughly one-third or more over time. Frequent keratoderma omitted at four-axis cap.
Relative polycythemia from dehydration-induced hemoconcentration; no additional intrinsic organ damage established.
Carnitine transport and fatty-acid oxidation disorders; muscle, cardiac and hepatic injury vary substantially by subtype and are not established across most of this umbrella.
PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy directly affects ventricular myocardium and cardiac rhythm.
Fatal cerebral neurodegeneration caused by a transmissible prion agent; sleep and oculomotor abnormalities reflect CNS disease.
Hemolytic stomatocytosis, glucose transport dysfunction and syndromic CNS impairment; cataracts occur in 30-79%. Reported hepatic abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.
Isolated inherited early-onset cataract affects the lens.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 20/20 patients.
CACNA1F-related retinal dysfunction or dystrophy; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular CNS damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 7/7; seizures in 4/7. Minor digital shape changes do not establish functional skeletal damage; obesity alone adds no endocrine axis.
Astrocytic tumour arising in the brainstem.
Congenital shortening of the fourth metatarsal is a skeletal abnormality.
Luteinized ovarian stromal cells produce excess androgens; this is a disorder of gonadal endocrine function.
Familial susceptibility to breast cancer; breast has no axis, and susceptibility alone establishes no damage elsewhere.
Descriptor supports congenital skeletal and digital malformations; no definition or phenotype evidence supports additional organs.
Direct toxic or nutritional injury to the optic nerve, assigned to the ocular axis; inflammatory ancestry does not establish immune causation.
Neurodegenerative PSP variant defined by akinesia and gait freezing; motor and speech abnormalities arise from CNS dysfunction.
Skeletal dysplasia with limb shortening and elbow dislocation. Intellectual disability and cardiovascular malformations are occasional, below 30%.
Malignancy of the glans penis is assigned to the reproductive organ of origin, which has no axis.
Defined by neurofibromatosis, adrenal pheochromocytoma and duodenal carcinoid; cutaneous neurofibromas affect most adults with the associated NF1 phenotype.
Recurrent inflammatory anterior uveitis with elevated intraocular pressure; viral infection, particularly CMV, underlies a substantial subset.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining destructive encephalopathy. Respiratory failure does not establish intrinsic lung injury; muscle enzyme defects alone do not establish myopathy.
Developmental delay, congenital heart defects and limb abnormalities define the syndrome. Hearing impairment occurs in 2/7, below 30%.
Pooling and sequestration of blood cells in the spleen; spleen as a blood organ belongs to the haematologic axis.
Familial febrile seizure disorder affects neuronal excitability; fever does not establish an intrinsic infectious or immune disease.
